mechanism: exact in substance, one wording slip and one missing scope condition. Reproduced independently in the project container (fresh regtest wallet in a temp datadir, driven through rpc-createwallet / rpc-encryptwallet): all 8 walletdescriptorkey rows carry the SAME 32-byte master secret; before encryptwallet it is in the WAL (000003.log at offset 188), after encryptwallet it is in a live SST (000005.ldb at offset 4439) together with the whole DER record value, and it is still there after two more bl.store:leveldb-compact calls on the same handle. The precise mechanism is one step off from the finding's wording: leveldb 1.23 DBImpl::CompactRange computes max_level_with_files over levels >= 1 BEFORE it flushes the memtable, so on a wallet with no SST files yet it gets 1; the flush that follows goes through WriteLevel0Table -> PickLevelForMemTableOutput, which -- finding nothing to overlap -- places the new table directly at LEVEL 2 (kMaxMemCompactLevel), not at level 0; the loop then compacts only levels [0,1), which are empty. So the surviving file is the memtable-FLUSH output pushed to the top level, not 'the compaction OUTPUT'. Confirmed directly: leveldb.stats after encryptwallet reports 1 file at level 2 and none below, and the LOG reads 'Level-0 table #5: 14068 bytes OK' followed by 'Manual compaction at level-0 ... (begin)..(end)' and nothing at level 2. The finding also omits the scope condition: the leak needs the plaintext to still be in the memtable AND the LSM to have no other files. With 4,000 junk 2KB records written first (8MB, levels populated) the post-encryption compact DOES erase the secret (hits NIL), and so does encrypting a wallet that has been unloaded and reloaded once (log replay puts the creation batch in a level-0 file, which then merges down and drops the tombstoned rows). Everything under that ceiling leaks: 200 getnewaddress calls before encrypting still leaked.
consequence: holds, and is stronger than the finding states. The wallet directory keeps the master xpub in a LIVE walletdescriptor record (generate-wallet-descriptor-string stores wpkh(<master xpub>/84h/1h/0h/0/*)), so directory + leaked 32 bytes = the complete master extended private key. Executed end to end: took two addresses from a fresh wallet, ran encryptwallet, then -- using only what the directory holds and no passphrase -- rebuilt the tprv from the stored xpub's chain code plus the bytes scraped out of 000005.ldb (bip32-neuter of the rebuilt key equals the stored xpub exactly), spliced it into the public descriptor and called deriveaddresses: the first two derived addresses are byte-for-byte the two the wallet had handed out, and getaddressinfo on the encrypted wallet still reports ismine=true for them, so they keep receiving. That is an attacker with a copy of the directory recovering spendable keys without the passphrase = S1. One correction to the finding's impact wording: the pre-encryption SPKMs stay loaded and ismine but are NOT signable while locked -- spkm-privkey-provider (wallet.lisp:367-383) returns NIL for a pre-encryption keyid on the locked wallet and the right secret after walletpassphrase, so the in-memory half of encryption is correct; the break is purely on disk. Core's side of the comparison holds up: SQLiteDatabase::Rewrite runs VACUUM, and with secure_delete off (upstream's default, the case Core's 'slack space' comment is written for) a probe in the container showed DELETE leaves the secret in wallet.dat and VACUUM removes it, with no -journal or -wal file left behind (Core sets no journal_mode pragma). So Core's mechanism really does erase; ours does not. Note that Core has NO test for this: wallet_encryption.py never inspects the file, and grep finds no 'slack'/'VACUUM' assertion anywhere in test/ or src/wallet/test/. Ours has no such test either, and the one test that looks like a control -- tests/storage/storage-tests.lisp:787 leveldb-compact-preserves-data -- only checks the LOGICAL view (leveldb-get returns NIL), which is true whether or not the bytes are gone.
evidence: Ours: src/wallet/wallet-crypt.lisp:402-408 (the handler-case around bl.store:leveldb-compact, whose own comment already concedes 'This is NOT an erasure guarantee'), src/kv/leveldb.lisp:405-411 (leveldb-compact = CompactRange(NULL,NULL); its docstring's 'merges every level and physically drops deleted/overwritten keys' is false for the topmost level with files -- it repeats leveldb db.h:137-147's own claim), src/wallet/wallet.lisp:702-717 (the stored descriptor carries the master xpub) and :762-800 (one master-priv shared by all 8 SPKMs). Core: refs/bitcoin/src/wallet/wallet.cpp:874-876 (the 'slack space' comment + GetDatabase().Rewrite()), refs/bitcoin/src/wallet/sqlite.cpp:336-341 (VACUUM). Probes, all in the project container: (1) fresh wallet -> BEFORE hits=((000003.log . 188)), AFTER encryptwallet hits=((000005.ldb . 4439)), after 2nd and 3rd compact on the same handle hits unchanged; record counts (plain,ckey,mkey) 8,0,0 -> 0,16,1. (2) leveldb.stats after encryptwallet = 'Level 2: 1 file' with nothing at 0 or 1; LOG shows 'Level-0 table #5: 14068 bytes OK' then 'Manual compaction at level-0' only. (3) CompactRange with EXPLICIT begin/end keys (00 .. ff*64, via bl.kv::%leveldb-compact-range) -> hits unchanged; leveldb/c.h exposes only leveldb_compact_range, there is no per-level manual-compaction entry point to reach for. (4) WAL: after encryptwallet 000004.log is 0 bytes and the log-file scan is NIL, so the survivor is the SST, not the WAL. (5) unload -> hits unchanged; reload -> hits unchanged; reopen + compact -> hits NIL (the finder's positive control, reproduced). (6) 4,000 x 2KB junk records before encrypting -> AFTER hits NIL; one unload/reload before encrypting -> AFTER hits NIL; 200 getnewaddress before encrypting -> AFTER hits ((000005.ldb . 96832)). (7) consequence probe: pre-encryption addresses bcrt1q7xalgkuk857wra5pu7qyzmedz2mpk63kjqardk / bcrt1qyzc3x5p99pumhs3eg6jtm9cm5u5mwwrn6kk696, secret 9e7379ea...273a scraped from 000005.ldb, rebuilt tprv neuters to the stored tpub, deriveaddresses [0,3] returns both addresses first, ismine=T, wallet locked. (8) locked-signing probe: spkms 8 -> 16 after encryption, locked lookup NIL, unlocked lookup = the pre-encryption secret. (9) Core model: sqlite 3.46.1, PRAGMA secure_delete=0, insert -> hit, DELETE -> still a hit, VACUUM -> no hit, no journal file left.
fix_shape: Core's Rewrite is a whole-file REBUILD (VACUUM for sqlite, copy-to-temp-then-rename for BDB), so the faithful analogue for a LevelDB-backed wallet is to rewrite the database, not to compact it. After the encryption batch commits and the seed rotation finishes, iterate the live records into a brand-new LevelDB directory beside the wallet (wallets/<name>.rewrite/), fsync it, close both handles, atomically rename the new directory over the old one, delete the old, and reopen the wallet on the new handle -- with the whole thing under the wallet lock and crash-ordered so that an interruption leaves either the old complete encrypted wallet or the new one. The already-present record iterator (wallet-db-records) and wallet-db-open give the primitives; backupwallet/restorewallet already round-trip the same record set, so the shape exists in tree. What must NOT be shipped as the fix is the cheap-looking 'close, reopen, compact': probe (5) only erases because reopening replays a non-empty log into an overlapping level-0 file that then merges into level 2, and probe (7)'s raw reopen shows the same dependency -- with an empty log at reopen the compaction is a no-op again, and the failure is silent. If a rewrite is judged too heavy for now, the interim must at least verify (scan the SSTs, or read back through a fresh handle) rather than assume. Whatever is chosen, the regression test has to byte-scan the wallet directory for the secret after encryptwallet: the existing tests/storage/storage-tests.lisp:787 leveldb-compact-preserves-data checks only the logical view and stays green through this bug. Separately, correct the leveldb-compact docstring at src/kv/leveldb.lisp:405-411 -- the topmost level with files is never rewritten, which also weakens the disk-reclamation promise its other two callers rely on (src/node/reindex.lisp:107, src/storage/coins-view-cache.lisp:120-124).
